correctness.rationale: Represent each ideal by its chain prefix lengths in {0,...,L}, with sum of prescribed parity. Two queries in a chain forbid the nonmonotone trace; an unused chain supplies either parity via lengths 0 and 1. For a full transversal the response intervals are [0,j-1] and [j,L]. An interior height gives both parities for either response. At endpoint heights only the all-singleton choice can fail, and its total length is L times the number of top queries. This gives precisely the deleted facets, polynomial, and VC dimension. The undeleted join X has a free top reduced group of rank (L-1)^k and no other reduced groups. For L>=3, use an interior reference vertex in each chain: the join of differences of the missing facet's vertices with the reference vertices is a cycle evaluating to a signed unit on that relative facet and zero on every other omitted facet. Thus the top-to-relative map is onto over Z and its kernel is free of the displayed rank; no hidden lower group or torsion remains. For L=2 the join is the cross-polytope boundary. Deleting all its facets at odd parity leaves the old top boundary image as the new highest reduced homology, free of rank 2^k-1, with lower groups unchanged. The augmented calculation also gives H̃_{-1}=Z for k=1,L=2,p=1, and the vertex case for k=1,L>=3 agrees with the formula.
residual_risks: The finite rational-rank checks do not check torsion. Freeness and the dimension range are justified by the integral chain argument. No general homotopy-type assertion is certified.
